Municipal Planning Grant

The Municipal Planning Grant (MPG) program encourages and supports planning and revitalization for local municipalities in Vermont. Awarded annually and administered by the Department of Housing and Community Development, the MPG program works to strengthen Vermont by funding local planning initiatives that support statewide planning goals. Since 1998, the MPG program has provided over $17 million to 243 cities and towns across Vermont to help breathe new life into communities, plan for future growth and development, and improve the quality of life.

Applicant Guidance

All the documents and reference materials needed to successfully apply for a Municipal Planning Grant are available below.  $1.2 million is available for grants in FY27.

Program Description & Application Guide

  • 2027 Program Description (PDF) - A helpful guide to understand the Municipal Planning Grant program.
  • 2027 Application Guide (DOC) - An application guide, that allows you to prepare your responses offline, review scoring criteria, and get helpful tips.
  • Rural Towns List (PDF) - A list of towns eligible to have the Regional Planning Commission serve as an agent of the town for the MPG.
  • Very Small Town List (PDF) - A list of towns with 1,000 residents or fewer, who will have no match requirement for Municipal Plans / Bylaws in towns that do not currently have them.
  • MPG Map of Awards (PDF) - This map represents all Municipal Planning Grant award distribution throughout the State in the past five years.

Accessing and Using GEARS

  • Legacy GEARS - The legacy version of GEARS hosts all Municipal Planning Grants from 2024, and earlier.
  • GEARS-IGX - GEARS-IGX, is the newest version of GEARS, and hosts Municipal Planning Grants from 2025, 2026, 2027 and future rounds.
  • MPG Roles (PDF) - List of roles used in the GEARS system, and who at the municipality may hold them. We strongly recommend designating two individuals for the Municipal/Authorizing Official (M/AO) role and designating a grant administrator.
  • 2027 GEARS Online Application Instructions (PDF) - A helpful resource to guide you through the screens, steps, and submission process on the GEARS-IGX online grants management system

Additional Required Application Forms

  • Municipal Resolution - This document must be completed, signed by a majority of the City Council / Selectboard, and submitted with a MPG application.
  • Certificate of Good Standing - A self-certification that the applicant is in Good Standing with the Agency of Natural Resources and the Agency of Agriculture, Food, and Markets. This is a required part of the application.

Grant Closeout

The following information and documents are due when closing the Municipal Planning Grant. All information and documents must be uploaded into GEARS.

  • Final Report - The final report is found in GEARS, and is completed online.
  • Final Product - Copies of any final products as outlined in Attachment A of the grant agreement, must be uploaded into GEARS. All final products must include evidence that the Municipal Planning Grant program administered by the Department of Housing and Community Development, is credited for funding on the product itself.
  • Financial Information - The following financial information is required to be submitted.
    • Summary Ledger - The summary ledger serves as the cover sheet for all invoices/receipts, and is used to accurately maintain financial records throughout the grant term.
    • Invoices and Receipts - Copies of invoices and receipts for all project expenditures, including match funds, and one of the following:
      • Copies of all canceled checks; or
      • Detailed transaction report, which includes vendor name, date of payment, amount of payment, check number, and the report must be signed and certified by the treasurer as true and accurate.
    • Canceled checks, or the detailed transaction report must demonstrate that all invoices have been paid by the municipality.
  • GIS Work - If GIS work was done with grant funds, and if new data layers were created, please confer with the consultant and have them submit the new data layers via the online intake form.

2026 Program Evaluation

The 2026 Vermont Planning & Community Investment Survey Results (PDF) - The Division of Community Planning + Revitalization in the Department of Housing & Community Development produces a survey on Vermont planning and development topics every three years, including an evaluation of the Municipal Planning Grant program.  These results report on stakeholders’ planning and development priorities and help the Department of Housing & Community Development evaluate the Municipal Planning Grant (MPG) program for updates.  The Department thanks participants for their time as we continuously work to improve policies, programs, and projects that support Vermont.
